sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface and total expression quantified by ELISA on intact cells; Western blotting, co-immunoprecipitation, and time-resolved fluorescence (TRF) analysis performed; multiple independent studies confirm surface display with no reported functional impairment.
sites.rationale: Six independent ledger lines (L1–L6) all explicitly name the junction between residues 371 and 372 in full-length human CaSR as the insertion site for FLAG or Myc epitopes. Python verification confirms residue 371 = D and residue 372 = T, both within the extracellular span 20–612, 242 residues from the nearest TM boundary (613). The authors describe this as a 'functionally silent loop in the ECD', and the tagged constructs are used routinely for surface ELISA, co-IP, and TRF assays across multiple publications. Full-length human CaSR with FLAG (DYKDDDDK) or Myc (EQKLISEEDL) epitope inserted between residues 371 and 372 in the VFT domain ECD loop, transiently transfected in HEK-293 cells; described as a 'functionally silent loop in the ECD'.

sources.claim: ( 31 ) For the generation of suitable CaSR constructs, we used a WT human CaSR and a variant that had been modified by the insertion of a FLAG epitope tag DYKDDDDK in the receptor's VFT domain, between residues 371 and 372, ( 35 ) to permit quantitation of total and surface expression by ELISA.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: IP accumulation assay (L8): pEC50 for Ca2+ of 2.50 ± 0.02 (FLAG-SNAP-CaSR WT) vs 2.39 ± 0.03 (HA-CaSR WT) — no significant difference, confirming Gq/11 pathway activation is preserved. Surface expression confirmed by ELISA (L7) and FACS on intact cells (L13, L14).
sites.rationale: Multiple papers report N-terminal tags (FLAG-SNAP, HA) on full-length human CaSR that are accessible on the extracellular face of intact cells. CaSR has a signal peptide (residues 1–19) and a large extracellular N-terminus beginning at residue 20; the N-terminal tag must be placed after signal peptide cleavage (insert_after_residue = 19, residue_before = A, residue_after = Y). No residue is named in any clip, so the junction is topology-derived: the mature N-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus available. L8 demonstrates function is fully preserved (Ca2+-induced IP accumulation indistinguishable from HA-CaSR WT); L13/L14 confirm surface accessibility by FACS on intact cells. Full-length human CaSR with N-terminal FLAG-SNAP tag (L7–L9, PMID 31399503) and N-terminal HA tag (L13–L14, DOI 10.1101/2024.07.08.602375) expressed in HEK293 cells; surface display confirmed by ELISA (L7) and FACS of intact non-permeabilized cells with PE-conjugated anti-HA antibody (L14). No specific residue is named; the junction is derived from the signal peptide cleavage site (residues 1–19) leaving the mature N-terminus at residue 20.

sources.claim: In a functional IP accumulation assay there was no difference in agonist potency of Ca 2 1 for thetwo receptor constructs (Fig. 1A;pEC values of 2.50 6 0.02 and 2.39 6 0.03 for FLAG-SNAP-CaSR WT and HACaSR WT, respectively), thereby confirming that the SNAP tag did not prevent Ca 2 1 -mediated activation of the G q/11 pathway.

literature_notes: L10 (Myc-tagged asCasr, axolotl CaSR ortholog) provides indirect support for the N-terminal site but names no residue and is an ortholog; it is subsumed by the direct human CaSR evidence in L7–L9 and L13–L14. L11 (EGFP-tagged CaSR, PMC9299317) reports plasma membrane localisation but names no position; EGFP fusions on GPCRs are most commonly C-terminal (intracellular in CaSR, residues 857–1078), so this clip cannot ground a surface site and no residue can be assigned. L12 (myc-tagged hCaSR, DOI 10.1101/2024.07.08.602375) confirms surface display by whole-cell immunisation but names no position; it is subsumed by the stronger L13/L14 evidence for the N-terminal site. The small extracellular loops ECL1 (668–679), ECL2 (745–770), and ECL3 (824–836) are not addressed by any ledger line and are therefore not proposed.
